did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ezra not only prayed over the people’s sins, but also wept, confessed, and fell facedown before the house of God. As a result, a large crowd of men, women, and children gathered around him.

Did you know? Shecaniah son of Jehiel, one of the descendants of Elam, said to Ezra, “There is still hope for Israel”—meaning that despite the unfaithfulness, he saw an opportunity for repentance and restoration.
Did you know? Following Shecaniah’s proposal, Ezra made the leaders of the priests and Levites, along with all Israel, swear to carry out the decision, and the people took the oath.
Did you know? Ezra withdrew to the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib and mourned while fasting. During that time, he ate no bread and drank no water because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles.
Did you know? Anyone who failed to come to Jerusalem within the appointed three days risked having all his property confiscated and being excluded from the assembly of the exiles.

Did you know? The assembly took place on the twentieth day of the ninth month, that is, Kislev, while the people sat in the square before the house of God, trembling because of the solemn occasion and the heavy rain.
Did you know? The people recognized that the task was too great to complete in a day or two, so they decided to examine the cases gradually and at set times.
Did you know? The examination began on the first day of the tenth month, Tebeth, and continued until the first day of the first month, Nisan.
Did you know? Among the priests found to have married foreign women were descendants of Jeshua son of Jehozadak. They pledged to divorce their wives and to offer a ram for their guilt.
Did you know? At the end of the list, it says that all the men named had married foreign women, and that some of them had children by those marriages.
